text:
alicia: ran `npm audit` against main (console/ui) after the assets merge — saw a couple of worrying hits and a lot of lockfile churn. posting summary, need quick triage :lock:

alicia: audit highlights:
```
# npm audit report
node-forge  <=0.10.0  prototype pollution / crypto integrity issue
Severity: high
Path: console-ui > console-shared-crypto > node-forge

follow-redirects  1.x  redirect header injection (medium)
Path: console-ui > some-legacy-fetch > follow-redirects
```

dependabot: Dependabot created PR #342: "bump node-forge to 0.10.2"

sam: thanks — do we know if node-forge actually ends up in the browser bundle or only in our server-side helpers?

mohit: quick look: node-forge is imported by `console-shared/crypto` which is used by server KMS shim and also accidentally re-exported in `console-client` index. that re-export path is tree-shaken in most builds but the SSR build (Next) pulls it into the server bundle. so runtime exposure is mostly server-side, but we do ship it to some CI runners.

alicia: so impact: likely not a direct XSS in user browsers, but it could be abused on servers running SSR or on dev machines that run vulnerable scripts. recommends patch asap.

sam: options? upgrade, rewrite to WebCrypto, or do a temporary patch? lockfile churn is a concern for product (too many changed files).

mohit: upgrade to 0.10.2 is the clean fix if the patch is non-breaking. alternative quick mitigations:
- use `resolutions` / pnpm overrides to force patched version (less churn if we do exact pin)
- patch-package to neutralize the vulnerable function at build time (fast, dirty)
- remove the accidental re-export from `console-client` (low risk, stops bundling)

jane: priority decision: because the vulnerable code can run on our SSR nodes and CI runners, mark P1 for immediate remediation. we should avoid long-lived workarounds.

alicia: plan proposal:
1) open hotfix branch: `hotfix/node-forge-patch` (I'll do)
2) add `resolutions` to root package.json to pin node-forge@0.10.2 + run `pnpm install --lockfile-only` to minimize churn
3) small PR that removes the accidental re-export from console-client (quick follow-up)
4) run full CI and smoke on canary; if passes, backport to release-1.3.x and cut patch release

ci-bot: build failing on branch due to lockfile mismatch (pnpm v7 vs v8 differences) — ensure CI uses same pnpm version as local dev.

mohit: note on lockfile policy: to minimize churn let's prefer `--lockfile-only` with exact pins and avoid running `pnpm install` that regenerates top-level metadata. also we should commit only the minimal changed lock entries (but CI will include the full file).

sam: do we need a public customer notice? any data-exposure risk?

jane: no customer-facing breach; just an internal security advisory if we find SSR nodes were hit. ops will check logs. create an incident ticket if we see any sign of exploitation.

alicia: opening PR now. tagging @eng-sre and @releases for release coordination. will attach audit output and a short changelog.

mohit: follow-up: after hotfix, I'll add a tech-debt ticket to replace `console-shared/crypto` with a WebCrypto-based impl (target 2 sprints).

alicia: thanks everyone. ping me in thread if you want to pair on the PR. :thumbsup:
